The two existing Tamamoro Shrines are both considered {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} candidates mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} as "Tamamoro Shrine, {{ill|Yamanashi District|de|Yamanashi-gun|ja|山梨郡|zh|山梨郡|qid=Q11469930}}, {{ill|Kai Province|en|Kai Province|qid=Q858076|lt=Kai Province}}."
* 1. {{ill|Tamamoro Shrine|ja|玉諸神社|qid=Q11572792}} ({{ill|Kōfu|ar|كوفو (ياماناشي)|arz|كوفو|az|Kofu|azb|کوفو، یاماناشی|ban|Kōfu|be|Кофу (горад)|bg|Кофу|ca|Kōfu|ce|Кофу (гӀала)|ceb|Kōfu-shi (distrito)|cs|Kófu|de|Kōfu|eo|Kofu|es|Kōfu (Yamanashi)|et|Kōfu|eu|Kōfu|fa|کوفو (یاماناشی)|fi|Kōfu|fr|Kōfu|ga|Kōfu|gl|Kōfu, Yamanashi|he|קופו|hy|Կոֆու (քաղաք)|id|Kōfu, Yamanashi|it|Kōfu|ja|甲府市|ka|კოფუ|ko|고후시|lt|Kofu|mg|Kōfu|mzn|کوفو، یاماناشی|nl|Kofu|no|Kōfu|pl|Kōfu|pt|Kōfu|ro|Kōfu, Yamanashi|ru|Кофу (город)|sc|Kōfu|sh|Kōfu|simple|Kōfu|sr|Кофу|su|Kofu, Yamanashi|sv|Kōfu|sw|Kofu, Yamanashi|szl|Kōfu|tg|Кофу|th|โคฟุ|tl|Kōfu, Yamanashi|tr|Kōfu|tt|Кофу (шәһәр)|tum|Kōfu|uk|Кофу (Яманасі)|ur|کوفو، یاماناشی|vi|Kōfu, Yamanashi|war|Kōfu, Yamanashi|wuu|甲府市|zh|甲府市|zh_classical|甲府市|zh_min_nan|Kôhu-chhī|zh_yue|甲府|qid=Q201932|lt=Kofu}}, Kokudama Town) – Recognized as the {{ill|Sannomiya|eu|Sannomiya|fa|ساننومیا|ja|三宮|ko|산노미야|ru|Санномия|th|ซันโนะมิยะ|zh|三宮|qid=Q7418864|lt=third-Ranked shrine}} of Kai Province; former {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.
* 2. {{ill|Tamamoro Shrine|ja|玉諸神社|qid=Q11572792}} ({{ill|Kōshū, Yamanashi|ar|كوشو ياماناشي|azb|کوشو، یاماناشی|ca|Kōshū|ce|Косю|ceb|Kōshū-shi|de|Kōshū|eo|Koŝu|es|Kōshū|fa|کوشو، یاماناشی|fi|Kōshū|fr|Kōshū|gl|Kōshū|hy|Կոսյու|id|Kōshū, Yamanashi|it|Kōshū|ja|甲州市|ko|고슈시|mzn|کوشو، یاماناشی|nl|Koshu (Yamanashi)|no|Kōshū (Yamanashi)|pl|Kōshū|ro|Kōshū|ru|Косю|sv|Kōshū|tl|Kōshū, Yamanashi|tr|Kōshū|tt|Косю|uk|Косю|vi|Kōshū, Yamanashi|war|Kōshū, Yamanashi|zh|甲州市|zh_classical|甲州市|zh_min_nan|Kôsyû-chhī|zh_yue|甲州|qid=Q248723|lt=Koshu}}, Shioyama Takemori) – Former {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

These two shrines have completely different enshrined deities and origins. The name "Tamamoro" at the Kofu shrine originates from the former sacred tree "Tamamuro Cedar," while at the Koshu shrine, it derives from the shrine’s former sacred object, a crystal sphere.

According to the *Shikinaisha Research Report*, the Koshu shrine was founded on an ancient belief in sacred stones, as scattered quartz fragments and residential remains are still visible in the area. This also connects to the listing of "Tamai District" in the {{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|ja|和名抄|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 和名類聚抄|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2702542}}. On the other hand, the Kofu shrine was historically venerated as a "Kokudama Shrine," deriving its name from the enshrined deity "Kunidama no Kami" (國魂神). However, the connection between the "tama" (玉) in Tamamoro and the "tama" in Kunidama is considered tenuous.<ref name=chosa>*Shikinaisha Research Report*, Tamamoro Shrine section.</ref>

It is recognized as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} and as the {{ill|Sannomiya|eu|Sannomiya|fa|ساننومیا|ja|三宮|ko|산노미야|ru|Санномия|th|ซันโนะมิยะ|zh|三宮|qid=Q7418864|lt=third shrine}} of {{ill|Kai Province|en|Kai Province|qid=Q858076|lt=Kai Province}}. Its former status was a {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Okuninushi}} (Referred to as Kunidama Ōkami-no-Mikoto)

The *Kai Kokushi* identifies the enshrined deity as Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto (大己貴命).

=== History ===
[[File:御室山 (甲府市).JPG|thumb|200px|right|Mt. Omuro]]

According to shrine tradition, the deity was originally enshrined on Mount Omuro, north of {{ill|Sakaori-no-Miya|ja|酒折宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11644327}}. Later, when {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}} passed through the region on his eastern expedition, he buried a sacred jewel at the present site, planted a cedar tree over it as a sacred object, and enshrined Kunidama Ōkami to prevent flooding. The floodwaters receded, and a shrine was eventually built there. The sacred tree, known as the "Tamamuro Cedar," is said to have given rise to the name "Tamamoro."<ref>From the shrine’s information board.</ref> The surrounding area of Kokudama (くだま) is also named after the shrine.

The genealogy of the {{ill|Kai no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|甲斐国造|lt=Kai Kokuzo}} records that the second-generation chief, Hayahiko-no-Sukune (速彦宿禰), enshrined "Tamano-o-Kami."<ref>{{ill|Norinobu Nakata|ja|中田憲信|qid=Q140447354}}, "Kai Kokuzo," *Shokeifu* Vol. 7.</ref>

The former site of the shrine’s main hall, located at the foot of Mount Omuro, is considered a relic of an ancient {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site}}. Since Mount Omuro is still visible from the current location, it is believed that the shrine originated as a place of worship for the mountain.<ref name=kamigami>*Japanese Deities* (日本の神々), Tamamoro Shrine section.</ref> Several sacred rock formations (iwakura) remain on the mountain, and numerous ancient tombs and archaeological sites dot the area. A yamamiya (mountain shrine) once existed at the summit, and there are accounts of ancient processions ascending the mountain.

During the Edo period, the shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Tokugawa clan|en|Tokugawa clan|qid=Q1412769|lt=Tokugawa clan}}, and its lands were confirmed with a stipend of 61 koku.<ref>*Geographical Names of Yamanashi Prefecture* (山梨県の地名), Kofu City, Tamamoro Shrine section.</ref>

In 1922, the shrine was elevated to Prefectural Shrine status under the modern shrine Ranking system.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Ama-no-Hakarudama-no-Mikoto|ja|天羽明玉命}}

Some sources list the deity as "Ama-no-Akarutama-no-Mikoto" or "{{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|en|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|qid=Q11572729|lt=Tamanooya-no-Mikoto}}."

=== History ===
The shrine’s founding date is unknown. The area has long been known for quartz production, and historical records in the *Wamyosho* mention "Tamai District." It is believed that the shrine originated from gemstone worship.<ref name=chosa/>

The original sacred object was a massive crystal sphere, but it was stolen in the early Meiji period.
